title: Two-colour profile convolution for uniform partition coefficients
statement:
Let $n\geq0$ and $m\geq1$ be integers, and let $a,b\geq0$ satisfy $a+b=nm$. Define the finite set
$$R_{n,m,a}=\{(r_0,\ldots,r_m)\in\mathbb N^{m+1}:\sum_{i=0}^m r_i=n,\ \sum_{i=0}^m i r_i=a\}.$$
For $r\in R_{n,m,a}$ put
$$C_{a,b}(r)=\frac{a!b!}{\prod_{i=0}^m r_i!(i!)^{r_i}((m-i)!)^{r_i}}\in\mathbb Q.$$
Each $C_{a,b}(r)$ is a nonnegative integer, and
$$\sum_{r\in R_{n,m,a}}C_{a,b}(r)=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}.$$
Here $0!=1$, empty sums and products have their usual values, and all quotients are computed in the rational field $\mathbb Q$ [def-weil-field]; the assertion includes integrality of the displayed sum.

proof.text: If $n=0$, then $a=b=0$ and every $r_i=0$; there is exactly one profile, its coefficient is $1$, and the right side is $1$. Hence assume $n>0$. Choose disjoint labelled sets $U,V$ of cardinalities $a,b$, and let $E=U\sqcup V$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the finite set of partitions of $E$ into $n$ unordered blocks of size $m$: a partition is a collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets whose union is $E$. For $P\in\mathcal P$, let $r_i(P)$ be the number of blocks containing exactly $i$ elements of $U$. Counting blocks and then elements of $U$ gives $\sum r_i(P)=n$ and $\sum i r_i(P)=a$. Thus $\rho(P)=(r_i(P))$ belongs to $R_{n,m,a}$. This profile set is finite since $0\leq r_i\leq n$. Write $\mathcal P_r=\{P:\rho(P)=r\}$.

proof.text: Fix $r\in R_{n,m,a}$. Make slots $(i,h)$ with $0\leq i\leq m$ and $1\leq h\leq r_i$, in lexicographic order. There are $n$ slots; their red capacities are $i$ and their blue capacities are $m-i$. These total $a$ and $\sum(m-i)r_i=mn-a=b$. Let $\mathcal L$ consist of pairs of lists, one listing each element of $U$ exactly once and one listing each element of $V$ exactly once. Fix reference lists: permuting their labels gives bijections from $\operatorname{Perm}(U)$ and $\operatorname{Perm}(V)$ to the respective list sets. By [lem-sfb-finite-permutation-cardinality], $|\mathcal L|=a!b!$. Cut the red list into successive chunks with the red slot capacities, and the blue list with the blue capacities. In each slot unite its two chunks and forget their order and the slot labels. This defines $q_r:\mathcal L\to\mathcal P_r$: the resulting blocks are disjoint, cover $E$, and have size $m\geq1$, so they are nonempty and distinct.

source.place: Tag 07GP (lemma-check-on-generators), proof of (5) for x+y, final universal coefficient comparison; explicit combinatorial refinement written by Q36.

proof.text:
For any fixed $P\in\mathcal P_r$, a list pair over $P$ is specified uniquely as follows. For each $i$, biject the $r_i$ slots of type $i$ with the $r_i$ blocks of $P$ of that type; then choose a linear order of the red part and of the blue part of every assigned block. Concatenating those ordered parts in slot order recovers the two lists. Conversely cutting any list pair over $P$ recovers exactly these assignments and orders, so these constructions are inverse. There are $r_i!$ assignments (fix one assignment and compose with permutations), and $i!$ and $(m-i)!$ orders in each such block, by [lem-sfb-finite-permutation-cardinality]. Independent choices therefore give
$$|q_r^{-1}(P)|=D_r:=\prod_{i=0}^{m}r_i!(i!)^{r_i}((m-i)!)^{r_i}.$$
This is positive; empty colour parts have one order, since $0!=1$. In particular every $P$ has a preimage. The factor $r_i!$ permutes whole blocks, including the pure-colour blocks; no empty block is being counted.

source.place: Tag 07GP (lemma-check-on-generators), proof of (5) for x+y, final universal coefficient comparison; explicit combinatorial refinement written by Q36.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-finite-fibre-cardinality-sum] to $q_r$, with finite source $\mathcal L$ and target $\mathcal P_r$. Every fibre has size $D_r$, hence
$$a!b!=|\mathcal L|=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_r}D_r=|\mathcal P_r|D_r.$$
The source is nonempty (choose any two orders), so the equality also rules out an empty $\mathcal P_r$. Since $D_r>0$, division in $\mathbb Q$ gives $C_{a,b}(r)=|\mathcal P_r|$. This proves the nonnegative-integrality assertion for every profile.

source.place: Tag 07GP (lemma-check-on-generators), proof of (5) for x+y, final universal coefficient comparison; explicit combinatorial refinement written by Q36.

proof.text:
Now let $\mathcal O$ be the set of lists of all elements of $E$, each occurring once. Its cardinality is $(nm)!$ by [lem-sfb-finite-permutation-cardinality], using a reference list as above. Cut such a list into $n$ consecutive chunks of length $m$ and forget orders to obtain $q:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$. For any $P\in\mathcal P$, its preimages are specified uniquely by an ordering of its $n$ blocks and, independently, an ordering of the $m$ elements of every block: concatenate these lists to reconstruct the preimage. The cited permutation count gives $n!(m!)^n$ such choices. Applying [lem-sfb-finite-fibre-cardinality-sum] to this map yields
$$(nm)!=|\mathcal P|n!(m!)^n,\qquad |\mathcal P|=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}$$
in $\mathbb Q$. Both maps land in their stated finite targets by their explicit cutting constructions; no surjectivity or partition-count formula has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 07GP (lemma-check-on-generators), proof of (5) for x+y, final universal coefficient comparison; explicit combinatorial refinement written by Q36.

proof.text:
Finally apply [lem-sfb-finite-fibre-cardinality-sum] to $\rho:\mathcal P\to R_{n,m,a}$. Its fibres are exactly $\mathcal P_r$ by definition, and step 1 verified the target condition. Substituting step 4, then step 5, gives
$$\sum_{r\in R_{n,m,a}}C_{a,b}(r)=\sum_{r\in R_{n,m,a}}|\mathcal P_r|=|\mathcal P|=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}.$$
The common value is a cardinality and hence a nonnegative integer. This completes both assertions, with the empty case supplied in step 1.

lean.statement: theorem colourProfile_coefficients (n m a b : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hab : a + b = n * m) : (∀ r ∈ (Finset.Nat.antidiagonalTuple (m + 1) n).filter (fun r ↦ ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (i : ℕ) * r i = a), ∃ c : ℕ, ((a.factorial * b.factorial : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((∏ i : Fin (m + 1), (r i).factorial * (i : ℕ).factorial ^ r i * (m - (i : ℕ)).factorial ^ r i : ℕ) : ℚ) = (c : ℚ)) ∧ (∑ r ∈ (Finset.Nat.antidiagonalTuple (m + 1) n).filter (fun r ↦ ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (i : ℕ) * r i = a), ((a.factorial * b.factorial : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((∏ i : Fin (m + 1), (r i).factorial * (i : ℕ).factorial ^ r i * (m - (i : ℕ)).factorial ^ r i : ℕ) : ℚ)) = (((n * m).factorial : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((n.factorial * m.factorial ^ n : ℕ) : ℚ)
